- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- In cases of recent strong upward moves (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate continuation — apply mean reversion bias toward prior 10-day average.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2), model often misreads momentum — adjust forecast by subtracting 2–3% of the recent 7-day average from the next 3–5 periods.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 30d moving average, reweight sentiment influence — higher sentiment = lower weight on short-term volatility.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate downside risk — add 1–2% buffer to forecast lows.  
- Avoid forecasting spikes after sentiment peaks — if sentiment peaks then drops, model often overreacts — cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior peak.
